title: Gym-Anything-RT: Scaling Real-Time Environments for Vision-Language Agents
title_zh: Gym-Anything-RT：为视觉-语言智能体扩展实时环境

paragraphs.en: AI agents have made substantial progress in domains where they have a non-trivial amount of time to deliberate between actions, such as mathematics, software engineering, and performing tasks on desktop applications. It is less clear how such models fare in settings that demand real-time interaction , such as playing a video game or operating a physical device. In these settings, the environment state may evolve as the agent is reasoning, or even as the underlying model is performing a forward pass. To gain insight into the real-time interaction capabilities of vision-language agents, we introduce Gym-Anything-RT . Our key idea is to construct visual minigames that demand a portfolio of capabilities required for interactive real-time settings. Gym-Anything-RT uses an agentic pipeline to automatically generate such environments based on a taxonomy of six capabilities required for real-time interaction, including the ability to perceive the environment and act under an evolving environment state. A key feature of Gym-Anything-RT is that it allows for controlled comparison of real-time interaction capabilities: we can run the same minigame in real time, or pause or slow down the environment to relax the requirement for real-time actions. We use Gym-Anything-RT to construct 100 real-time minigames and evaluate AI agents on them. We find large capability gaps in real-time interaction. For example, GPT-6 Astra (xHigh) achieves a pass rate of only 9.0% on the real-time minigames, which rises to 75.0% when the environment is paused. We also identify intriguing behaviors by the most powerful frontier agents: for instance, when given the ability to write code, these agents write code that bypasses the need to perceive and act in real time. We publicly release Gym-Anything-RT and the generated minigames to spur further research on AI agents in real-time interactive settings. 1 1 1 Code and data are available at https://github.com/gym-anything/gym-anything-rt .
paragraphs.zh: AI智能体在那些于行动之间拥有可观思考时间的领域（如数学、软件工程以及在桌面应用上执行任务）已取得长足进展。 然而，这类模型在要求实时交互的场景（如玩电子游戏或操作物理设备）中表现如何，仍不太清楚。 在这类场景中，环境状态可能在智能体推理的过程中，甚至在底层模型执行前向传播的过程中不断演化。 为了深入了解视觉-语言智能体的实时交互能力，我们提出了 Gym-Anything-RT。 我们的核心思路是构建一系列视觉小游戏，这些游戏需要综合运用实时交互场景所要求的多种能力。 Gym-Anything-RT 使用一个智能体化流水线，基于实时交互所需的六项能力分类体系自动生成此类环境，这些能力包括感知环境以及在不断演化的环境状态下采取行动的能力。 Gym-Anything-RT 的一个关键特性是它支持对实时交互能力进行可控比较：我们可以以实时方式运行同一小游戏，也可以暂停或减慢环境，从而放宽对实时行动的要求。 我们使用 Gym-Anything-RT 构建了 100 个实时小游戏，并在其上对 AI 智能体进行评估。 我们发现智能体在实时交互方面存在巨大的能力差距。 例如，GPT-6 Astra (xHigh) 在实时小游戏上的通过率仅为 9.0%，而当环境被暂停时，通过率可提升至 75.0%。 我们还发现了最强大的前沿智能体的一些有趣行为：例如，当被赋予编写代码的能力时，这些智能体会编写出能够绕过实时感知与行动需求的代码。 我们公开发布 Gym-Anything-RT 及其生成的小游戏，以推动 AI 智能体在实时交互环境中的进一步研究。1 1 1 代码与数据可在 https://github.com/gym-anything/gym-anything-rt 获取。

paragraphs.en: AI agents have made substantial progress in domains where they have time to deliberate between actions, such as mathematics ( DeepSeek-AI, 2025 ) , software engineering ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) , and performing tasks on desktop applications ( Yuan et al., 2026 ; Aggarwal et al., 2026 ; Jang et al., 2026 ) . However, these agents have a key limitation: they are slow, often taking more than ten seconds to choose a single action. This is acceptable when the environment waits for the agent, but not in settings that demand real-time interaction , such as playing a video game or operating a physical device ( Zhang et al., 2026 ; Black et al., 2025 ) . There, the environment keeps changing while the agent reasons, or even while the model performs a forward pass. By the time an action executes, it may no longer be valid, and the agent cannot react to what happened in the meantime.
paragraphs.zh: AI 智能体在可以在行动之间进行思考的领域取得了显著进展，例如数学（DeepSeek-AI, 2025）、软件工程（Jimenez et al., 2024），以及在桌面应用程序上执行任务（Yuan et al., 2026; Aggarwal et al., 2026; Jang et al., 2026）。 然而，这些智能体存在一个关键局限：它们速度很慢，选择单个动作往往需要超过十秒的时间。 当环境等待智能体时，这是可以接受的；但在需要实时交互的场景中则不可行，例如玩电子游戏或操作物理设备（Zhang et al., 2026; Black et al., 2025）。 在这些场景中，环境在智能体推理期间持续变化，甚至在模型执行一次前向传播期间也在变化。 等到某个动作被执行时，它可能已经不再有效，而智能体也无法对这期间发生的情况做出反应。

sents.zh: 在这些场景中，环境在智能体推理期间持续变化，甚至在模型执行一次前向传播期间也在变化。

sents.en: By the time an action executes, it may no longer be valid, and the agent cannot react to what happened in the meantime.
sents.zh: 等到某个动作被执行时，它可能已经不再有效，而智能体也无法对这期间发生的情况做出反应。

paragraphs.en: Existing evaluations shed little light on this limitation. Computer-use benchmarks wait for the agent between actions, so they never test acting under an evolving state ( Xie et al., 2024 ; Yuan et al., 2026 ; Aggarwal et al., 2026 ) . Video game benchmarks do run in real time. However, frontier models make little progress on them ( Zhang et al., 2026 ; Ying et al., 2026 ; Ouyang et al., 2026 ) . Furthermore, each game combines many capabilities, such as 3D spatial understanding, temporal reasoning, and learning unfamiliar controls, in a single fixed task. This makes it difficult to tell whether models fail because they are too slow or because they lack some other capabilities. Separating these two causes requires controlled comparisons that vary how much time an agent has to respond on the same task.
paragraphs.zh: 现有的评估几乎无法揭示这一局限性。 计算机使用基准会在动作之间等待智能体，因此它们从不测试在状态不断变化下的行动能力（Xie et al., 2024；Yuan et al., 2026；Aggarwal et al., 2026）。 视频游戏基准确实是在实时环境中运行的。 然而，前沿模型在这些基准上几乎没有进展（Zhang et al., 2026；Ying et al., 2026；Ouyang et al., 2026）。 此外，每个游戏将多种能力——例如三维空间理解、时序推理以及学习陌生操作——组合在一个固定的单一任务中。 这使得我们难以判断模型失败究竟是因为它们反应太慢，还是因为它们缺乏其他某些能力。 要区分这两个原因，就需要进行受控比较，即在相同任务上改变智能体可用于响应的时间长短。

sents.zh: 现有的评估几乎无法揭示这一局限性。

sents.zh: 要区分这两个原因，就需要进行受控比较，即在相同任务上改变智能体可用于响应的时间长短。

paragraphs.en: To address these challenges, we introduce Gym-Anything-RT , a framework for creating environments for studying the real-time interaction capabilities of vision-language agents. Our key idea is to construct visual minigames that demand a portfolio of capabilities required for interactive real-time settings, while avoiding the complexity of complete games. For instance, in Rotating On-Screen Keyboard (Figure 1 ), the agent must enter a code by clicking keys that keep moving in three-dimensional space between its observation and its action. Furthermore, we build an evaluation stack that controls the clock of each minigame, so we can run the same task live at its natural speed, slow it down to give the agent more time to respond, or pause it between observation and action to remove the need for real-time actions. Since each minigame is a program, we can also modify it, for instance, to remove its temporal dynamics or to increase its difficulty. By comparing an agent’s performance on these variants of the same task, we can tell whether it fails because it cannot act in time as the environment changes, or because the task is hard for other reasons.
paragraphs.zh: 为应对这些挑战，我们提出 Gym-Anything-RT，一个用于创建环境以研究视觉语言智能体实时交互能力的框架。 我们的核心思想是构建需要一整套交互式实时环境所需能力的视觉小游戏，同时避免完整游戏的复杂性。 例如，在 Rotating On-Screen Keyboard 中（图 1），智能体必须通过点击在三维空间中持续移动的按键来输入代码，这些按键位于其观察与其动作之间。 此外，我们构建了一个控制每个小游戏时钟的评估栈，因此我们可以按自然速度实时运行同一任务，也可以放慢速度给智能体更多响应时间，或者在观察与动作之间暂停任务，从而消除对实时动作的需求。 由于每个小游戏都是一个程序，我们还可以对其进行修改，例如移除其时间动态或增加其难度。 通过比较智能体在同一任务这些变体上的表现，我们可以判断其失败是因为无法在环境变化时及时行动，还是因为任务由于其他原因而困难。

paragraphs.en: Building such minigames by hand is laborious, since each needs its own visuals, dynamics, controls, and verifier. We therefore build an agentic pipeline that generates the minigames automatically. We first survey prior work on embodied agents ( Savva et al., 2019 ; Srivastava et al., 2021 ; Yang et al., 2025c ) , video games ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) , and computer use ( Cheng et al., 2024 ; Xie et al., 2024 ) to identify six capabilities required for real-time interaction, such as 3D visual understanding, temporal reasoning, and acting under an evolving environment state, and select minigames that cover the capabilities. We then build on the creator-auditor procedure of Gym-Anything ( Aggarwal et al., 2026 ) , in which one coding agent builds an environment and an independent agent audits it. In our setting, a creator agent implements each minigame as a program, and additionally writes an oracle solution that uses the program’s internal state to show that the task is solvable. Independent audit agents then test the minigame and report problems to the creator agent, which fixes them until the minigame behaves as intended. Finally, review agents label the capabilities that each minigame requires. Each program also defines four easier difficulty levels and a simplified interaction mode, which let us evaluate weaker models and study what makes a task hard.
paragraphs.zh: 手工构建这类小游戏非常费时费力，因为每个游戏都需要自己的视觉、动态、控制和验证器。 因此，我们构建了一个智能体流水线来自动生成这些小游戏。 我们首先调研了具身智能体（Savva et al., 2019；Srivastava et al., 2021；Yang et al., 2025c）、视频游戏（Zhang et al., 2026）和计算机使用（Cheng et al., 2024；Xie et al., 2024）方面的已有工作，以确定实时交互所需的六项能力，例如 3D 视觉理解、时序推理以及在不断变化的环境状态下采取行动，并选择覆盖这些能力的小游戏。 然后，我们在 Gym-Anything（Aggarwal et al., 2026）的创建者—审计者流程基础上进行构建，其中一个编码智能体负责构建环境，另一个独立的智能体对其进行审计。 在我们的设置中，创建者智能体将每个小游戏实现为一个程序，并额外编写一个先知（oracle）解法，该解法利用程序的内部状态来证明任务是可解的。 随后，独立的审计智能体测试该小游戏并向创建者智能体报告问题，创建者智能体进行修复，直到小游戏按预期运行。 最后，评审智能体为每个小游戏标注其所需的能力。 每个程序还定义了四个更简单的难度级别和一个简化交互模式，这使我们能够评估较弱的模型，并研究是什么使一个任务变得困难。

sents.en: Finally, review agents label the capabilities that each minigame requires.
sents.zh: 最后，评审智能体为每个小游戏标注其所需的能力。

sents.en: Each program also defines four easier difficulty levels and a simplified interaction mode, which let us evaluate weaker models and study what makes a task hard.
sents.zh: 每个程序还定义了四个更简单的难度级别和一个简化交互模式，这使我们能够评估较弱的模型，并研究是什么使一个任务变得困难。

paragraphs.en: Using this pipeline, we construct a benchmark of 100 real-time minigames and their non-real-time counterparts, and use it to evaluate frontier and open-weight models. We find that current agents perform poorly in real time. GPT-6 Astra (xHigh) solves only 9.0% of the real-time tasks, while it solves 66.0% of their non-real-time counterparts, which we obtain by modifying each program so that it no longer requires real-time interaction. Other models perform even worse: Claude Opus 5.5 (xHigh) and GPT-6 Luna (xHigh) solve only 5.0% and 1.0% of the real-time tasks, and the open-weight Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.5-9B solve only 1.0% and 0.0%, respectively. In addition, we find that for frontier models, the primary bottleneck is speed. On the same real-time tasks, slowing the environment by 64 × \times raises Astra’s pass rate from 9.0% to 57.0%, and pausing it raises the pass rate to 75.0%. Since we also control difficulty and the interaction interface, we further identify temporal reasoning and exploration of unfamiliar interfaces as additional sources of difficulty.
paragraphs.zh: 利用该流程，我们构建了一个包含 100 个实时小游戏及其非实时对应版本的基准，并用它来评估前沿模型和开放权重模型。 我们发现当前的智能体在实时场景下表现不佳。 GPT-6 Astra（xHigh）仅解决了 9.0% 的实时任务，而其非实时对应版本的任务解决率达到 66.0%；非实时版本是通过修改每个程序使其不再需要实时交互而得到的。 其他模型表现更差：Claude Opus 5.5（xHigh）和 GPT-6 Luna（xHigh）分别仅解决了 5.0% 和 1.0% 的实时任务，开放权重的 Qwen3.8-27B 和 Qwen3.5-9B 则分别仅解决了 1.0% 和 0.0%。 此外，我们发现对前沿模型而言，主要瓶颈在于速度。 在相同的实时任务上，将环境放慢 64 × \times 倍可使 Astra 的通过率从 9.0% 提升到 57.0%，而暂停环境则可将通过率提升到 75.0%。 由于我们还控制了难度和交互界面，我们进一步将时序推理和对陌生界面的探索确定为额外的难度来源。

paragraphs.en: Interestingly, we also find that frontier agents can partially offset their poor real-time capabilities through their strong coding and reasoning capabilities . Specifically, when we allow Astra to run code, it writes scripts that perceive and act on its behalf between its own responses. For instance, in Rotating On-Screen Keyboard, it locates the moving keys using image template matching and clicks them within 200 ms. As a result, its real-time pass rate rises from 9.0% to 31.0%.

paragraphs.en: In summary, our contributions are three-fold. First, we introduce Gym-Anything-RT , a framework that uses coding agents to automatically generate real-time visual minigames as programs, with oracle solutions and controlled difficulty and interaction. Its evaluation stack runs each minigame live, slowed down, or paused. Second, using Gym-Anything-RT , we construct a benchmark of 100 real-time minigames and their non-real-time counterparts for studying the real-time interaction capabilities of vision-language agents. Third, through extensive evaluations, we show that current agents perform poorly in real time, that speed is the primary bottleneck for frontier models, and that frontier agents can partially offset their slow responses by writing code.
paragraphs.zh: 总而言之，我们的贡献有三个方面。 首先，我们提出 Gym-Anything-RT，这是一个利用编码智能体自动生成实时视觉小游戏作为程序的框架，并提供标准答案解法以及可控的难度和交互。 其评估栈可以实时、减速或暂停地运行每个小游戏。 其次，我们基于 Gym-Anything-RT 构建了一个包含 100 个实时小游戏及其非实时对应版本的基准，用于研究视觉语言智能体的实时交互能力。 第三，通过大量评估，我们表明当前智能体在实时场景下表现不佳，速度是前沿模型的主要瓶颈，而前沿智能体可以通过编写代码部分弥补其响应缓慢的问题。

paragraphs.en: Our goal is to develop a suite of minigames that test the real-time interaction capabilities of vision-language agents in a controllable way. In particular, we construct minigames in which the time available to respond can be controlled while the underlying task stays the same. Formally, each minigame is an executable environment ℰ \mathcal{E} whose program defines its internal state, controls, and clock. At each step, the agent observes a screenshot o t o_{t} and issues mouse and keyboard actions a t a_{t} , while the environment keeps evolving as the agent chooses a t a_{t} . We say that a task requires real-time interaction when the agent must use recent visual evidence to choose an action for the state in which it will execute, so that changes during the delay between observation and action can reduce that action’s value (Appendix H ).
paragraphs.zh: 我们的目标是开发一组小游戏，以可控的方式测试视觉-语言智能体的实时交互能力。 具体而言，我们构建了一些小游戏，在底层任务保持不变的情况下，可以控制可用于响应的时间。 形式化地，每个小游戏都是一个可执行环境 ℰ \mathcal{E}，其程序定义了内部状态、控制方式和时钟。 在每一步中，智能体观察截图 o t o_{t} 并发出鼠标和键盘动作 a t a_{t}，而环境在智能体选择 a t a_{t} 的同时持续演化。 当智能体必须利用最近的视觉证据为其将要执行动作的状态选择一个动作，使得观察与动作之间延迟期间发生的变化可能降低该动作的价值时，我们称该任务需要实时交互（附录 H）。

paragraphs.en: Each minigame has ten configurations ℰ d , i \mathcal{E}_{d,i} , where d ∈ { 1 , … , 5 } d\in\{1,\ldots,5\} specifies the difficulty and i ∈ { simplified , full } i\in\{\mathrm{simplified},\mathrm{full}\} specifies the interaction mode. Each configuration can be run with a slowdown s s : live execution at its natural speed ( s = 1 s=1 ), slowed execution ( s > 1 s>1 ), in which the clock advances at 1 / s 1/s of its normal rate, and paused execution, in which the environment freezes until the agent acts. In addition, each real-time minigame has a non-real-time counterpart ℰ ¯ \bar{\mathcal{E}} , obtained through a minimal change to its timing (Section 2.3 ). Since a broken or unsolvable minigame would be counted as an agent failure, every configuration must also be solvable and objectively gradable. We construct these minigames with coding agents, that is, LLM agents that can write and run code and inspect screenshots in a sandbox. All agents are instances of GPT-6 Astra run through the Codex CLI. Each agent takes on one of four roles: survey agents collect candidate minigames, creator agents implement real-time versions of them, audit agents verify them, and review agents calibrate difficulty and annotate capabilities. Figure 2 summarizes this procedure.
paragraphs.zh: 每个小游戏有十个配置 ℰ d , i \mathcal{E}_{d,i} ，其中 d ∈ { 1 , … , 5 } d\in\{1,\ldots,5\} 指定难度， i ∈ { simplified , full } i\in\{\mathrm{simplified},\mathrm{full}\} 指定交互模式。 每个配置都可以以慢速系数 s s 运行：以自然速度实时运行（ s = 1 s=1 ）、慢速运行（ s > 1 s>1 ），即时钟以正常速率的 1 / s 1/s 推进；以及暂停运行，即环境冻结直到智能体行动。 此外，每个实时小游戏都有一个非实时对应版本 ℰ ¯ \bar{\mathcal{E}} ，通过对其中计时的最小改动得到（第 2.3 节）。 由于一个损坏或不可解的小游戏会被计为智能体失败，因此每个配置还必须是可解且可客观评分的。 我们使用编码智能体来构建这些小游戏，即能够在沙箱中编写和运行代码并查看截图的 LLM 智能体。 所有智能体都是通过 Codex CLI 运行的 GPT-6 Astra 实例。 每个智能体承担四种角色之一：调查智能体收集候选小游戏，创建智能体实现它们的实时版本，审计智能体验证它们，评审智能体校准难度并标注能力。 图 2 总结了这一流程。

paragraphs.en: We prompt survey agents to search prior work, public demonstrations, visual puzzles, online videos, and social media for challenges that satisfy four criteria: they can be formulated as self-contained minigames, require visual understanding and grounding, require actions through a visual interface, and have objectively verifiable outcomes. These include tasks that involve moving objects, hidden information, physical manipulation, or changes that occur between actions. For every source, the survey agent records its provenance, objective, visual structure, required interactions, temporal behavior, failure and recovery process, and information needed to verify success.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提示调查智能体去搜索先前的研究工作、公开演示、视觉谜题、在线视频和社交媒体，寻找满足以下四项标准的挑战：它们可以被表述为自包含的小游戏，需要视觉理解与定位，需要通过视觉界面执行操作，并且具有客观可验证的结果。 这些包括涉及移动物体、隐藏信息、物理操作或在动作之间发生变化等任务。 对于每个来源，调查智能体会记录其出处、目标、视觉结构、所需的交互、时间行为、失败与恢复过程，以及验证成功所需的信息。

paragraphs.en: We manually review the first 15 minigames and use them as quality standards for subsequent agent iterations. We select candidates with a traceable source, distinct visual and interaction requirements, an objectively gradable outcome, and meaningful mouse or keyboard actions. A source need not involve real-time interaction itself, since the creator agent develops its mechanic into a real-time task (Section 2.2 ). We exclude tasks dominated by OCR, static image classification, arithmetic, or question answering, since these tasks do not require the forms of visual interaction that we seek to measure.
paragraphs.zh: 我们人工审查了前 15 个小游戏，并将其作为后续智能体迭代的质量标准。 我们选择具备可追溯来源、独特的视觉与交互要求、可客观评分的结果，以及有意义的鼠标或键盘操作的候选任务。 来源本身不必涉及实时交互，因为创作智能体会将其机制发展为实时任务（第 2.2 节）。 我们排除以 OCR、静态图像分类、算术或问答为主的任务，因为这些任务不需要我们想要测量的那类视觉交互形式。

paragraphs.en: To construct a real-time minigame ℰ \mathcal{E} from a source P P , we build upon the creator-auditor procedure from Gym-Anything ( Aggarwal et al., 2026 ) , in which a creator agent builds each environment and independent audit agents verify it. In our setting, the creator agent writes a program that implements the minigame and exposes a common interface for screenshot observations as well as mouse and keyboard actions. Crucially, we ask the creator agent to turn the task posed by the source into one that requires real-time interaction, as defined above, whether or not the source itself does. Adding decorative motion, a countdown, or faster animation is not sufficient. For example, Rotating On-Screen Keyboard requires the agent to click keys that keep moving between observation and action.
paragraphs.zh: 为了从源 P P 构建实时小游戏 ℰ \mathcal{E}，我们在 Gym-Anything（Aggarwal et al., 2026）的创建者-审计者流程基础上进行构建，其中创建者智能体构建每个环境，独立的审计智能体验证该环境。 在我们的设定中，创建者智能体编写一个程序来实现小游戏，并为截图观测以及鼠标和键盘动作提供一个统一接口。 至关重要的是，我们要求创建者智能体将源所提出的任务转化为需要实时交互的任务（如上文所定义），无论源本身是否如此。 仅仅添加装饰性的动画、倒计时或更快的动画是不够的。 例如，旋转屏幕键盘要求智能体点击在观测与动作之间不断移动的按键。

sents.en: To construct a real-time minigame ℰ \mathcal{E} from a source P P , we build upon the creator-auditor procedure from Gym-Anything ( Aggarwal et al., 2026 ) , in which a creator agent builds each environment and independent audit agents verify it.
sents.zh: 为了从源 P P 构建实时小游戏 ℰ \mathcal{E}，我们在 Gym-Anything（Aggarwal et al., 2026）的创建者-审计者流程基础上进行构建，其中创建者智能体构建每个环境，独立的审计智能体验证该环境。

sents.en: In our setting, the creator agent writes a program that implements the minigame and exposes a common interface for screenshot observations as well as mouse and keyboard actions.
sents.zh: 在我们的设定中，创建者智能体编写一个程序来实现小游戏，并为截图观测以及鼠标和键盘动作提供一个统一接口。

sents.en: Crucially, we ask the creator agent to turn the task posed by the source into one that requires real-time interaction, as defined above, whether or not the source itself does.
sents.zh: 至关重要的是，我们要求创建者智能体将源所提出的任务转化为需要实时交互的任务（如上文所定义），无论源本身是否如此。

sents.en: Adding decorative motion, a countdown, or faster animation is not sufficient.
sents.zh: 仅仅添加装饰性的动画、倒计时或更快的动画是不够的。

sents.en: For example, Rotating On-Screen Keyboard requires the agent to click keys that keep moving between observation and action.
sents.zh: 例如，旋转屏幕键盘要求智能体点击在观测与动作之间不断移动的按键。

paragraphs.en: The creator agent implements the generator, interface, dynamics, action handling, and grader of ℰ \mathcal{E} . It also constructs an oracle solver that uses the privileged state of the environment to determine a valid solution and executes it through the same action space available to the agent. A successful oracle execution therefore demonstrates that the task is solvable and that its action and grading paths agree. The creator agent records the implementation, oracle trajectory, and visual and temporal evidence for these claims (Appendix B.1 ).
paragraphs.zh: 创建者智能体实现 ℰ \mathcal{E} 的生成器、接口、动力学、动作处理和评分器。 它还构建一个oracle求解器，利用环境的特权状态确定一个有效解，并通过智能体可用的同一动作空间执行该解。 因此，oracle的成功执行证明了该任务是可解的，并且其动作与评分路径是一致的。 创建者智能体记录实现、oracle轨迹以及支持这些主张的视觉和时间证据（附录 B.1 ）。

sents.en: The creator agent implements the generator, interface, dynamics, action handling, and grader of ℰ \mathcal{E} .
sents.zh: 创建者智能体实现 ℰ \mathcal{E} 的生成器、接口、动力学、动作处理和评分器。

sents.en: It also constructs an oracle solver that uses the privileged state of the environment to determine a valid solution and executes it through the same action space available to the agent.
sents.zh: 它还构建一个oracle求解器，利用环境的特权状态确定一个有效解，并通过智能体可用的同一动作空间执行该解。

sents.en: A successful oracle execution therefore demonstrates that the task is solvable and that its action and grading paths agree.
sents.zh: 因此，oracle的成功执行证明了该任务是可解的，并且其动作与评分路径是一致的。

sents.en: The creator agent records the implementation, oracle trajectory, and visual and temporal evidence for these claims (Appendix B.1 ).
sents.zh: 创建者智能体记录实现、oracle轨迹以及支持这些主张的视觉和时间证据（附录 B.1 ）。

paragraphs.en: Each implementation is then audited by a fresh audit agent that cannot modify the program. The audit agent inspects the code and evidence, runs the environment when necessary, and checks generation, solvability, rendering, action handling, grading, and recovery from failure. It also checks the real-time requirement itself, searching for shortcuts that would let an agent avoid acting in real time, such as a brake that halts the moving parts or periodic motion that permits a precomputed solution. The audit agent returns issues to the creator agent for revision, and the loop repeats until an audit passes.
paragraphs.zh: 随后，每个实现都会由一个无法修改程序的全新审计智能体进行审计。 审计智能体检查代码和证据，必要时运行环境，并检查生成、可解性、渲染、动作处理、评分以及故障恢复。 它还检查实时性要求本身，寻找能让智能体逃避实时行动的捷径，例如使运动部件停止的制动器，或允许预计算解法的周期性运动。 审计智能体将问题返回给创建智能体进行修改，该循环不断重复，直到审计通过为止。

sents.en: Each implementation is then audited by a fresh audit agent that cannot modify the program.
sents.zh: 随后，每个实现都会由一个无法修改程序的全新审计智能体进行审计。

sents.zh: 审计智能体检查代码和证据，必要时运行环境，并检查生成、可解性、渲染、动作处理、评分以及故障恢复。

sents.en: It also checks the real-time requirement itself, searching for shortcuts that would let an agent avoid acting in real time, such as a brake that halts the moving parts or periodic motion that permits a precomputed solution.
sents.zh: 它还检查实时性要求本身，寻找能让智能体逃避实时行动的捷径，例如使运动部件停止的制动器，或允许预计算解法的周期性运动。

sents.zh: 审计智能体将问题返回给创建智能体进行修改，该循环不断重复，直到审计通过为止。

paragraphs.en: A low pass rate on a real-time minigame does not by itself show that real-time interaction is the cause, since the underlying task may also be hard. We therefore construct, for each real-time minigame ℰ \mathcal{E} , a non-real-time counterpart ℰ ¯ \bar{\mathcal{E}} that poses the same task without requiring real-time interaction. The creator agent makes a minimal change to the timing of ℰ \mathcal{E} , while preserving its goal, controls, difficulty, and the information available to the agent. An independent audit agent then checks across all ten configurations that the two versions differ only in their timing. Comparing an agent on ℰ \mathcal{E} and ℰ ¯ \bar{\mathcal{E}} thus lets us separate the effect of the real-time requirement from the difficulty of the underlying task.
paragraphs.zh: 在实时小游戏中通过率低本身并不能说明实时交互是原因，因为底层任务本身也可能很难。 因此，我们为每个实时小游戏 ℰ \mathcal{E} 构建一个非实时对应版本 ℰ ¯ \bar{\mathcal{E}}，它提出相同的任务但不要求实时交互。 创作者智能体对 ℰ \mathcal{E} 的时间设定做最小的改动，同时保留其目标、操作方式、难度以及智能体可获得的信息。 然后由一个独立的审计智能体检查全部十个配置，确认两个版本仅在于时间设定上有所不同。 通过比较智能体在 ℰ \mathcal{E} 和 ℰ ¯ \bar{\mathcal{E}} 上的表现，我们便能将实时要求的影响与底层任务的难度区分开来。

sents.zh: 在实时小游戏中通过率低本身并不能说明实时交互是原因，因为底层任务本身也可能很难。

sents.zh: 创作者智能体对 ℰ \mathcal{E} 的时间设定做最小的改动，同时保留其目标、操作方式、难度以及智能体可获得的信息。

sents.zh: 然后由一个独立的审计智能体检查全部十个配置，确认两个版本仅在于时间设定上有所不同。

sents.zh: 通过比较智能体在 ℰ \mathcal{E} 和 ℰ ¯ \bar{\mathcal{E}} 上的表现，我们便能将实时要求的影响与底层任务的难度区分开来。

paragraphs.en: To also evaluate weaker models and study what makes a task hard, we construct easier variants of each minigame. We vary the difficulty d d and the interaction mode i i while holding the other and the random seed fixed, for both ℰ \mathcal{E} and its counterpart.
paragraphs.zh: 为了同时评估较弱的模型并研究是什么导致任务困难，我们为每个小游戏构建了更简单的变体。 对于 ℰ \mathcal{E} 及其对应版本，我们在保持另一个因素和随机种子不变的情况下，改变难度 d d 和交互模式 i i。

sents.en: To also evaluate weaker models and study what makes a task hard, we construct easier variants of each minigame.
sents.zh: 为了同时评估较弱的模型并研究是什么导致任务困难，我们为每个小游戏构建了更简单的变体。

sents.en: We vary the difficulty d d and the interaction mode i i while holding the other and the random seed fixed, for both ℰ \mathcal{E} and its counterpart.
sents.zh: 对于 ℰ \mathcal{E} 及其对应版本，我们在保持另一个因素和随机种子不变的情况下，改变难度 d d 和交互模式 i i。

paragraphs.en: A difficulty-review agent first reads the generator, visible interface, grader, verifier, and oracle solver to determine what the original minigame requires. It compares this configuration with an approved set of reference minigames and assigns it to one of five levels. The creator agent preserves the original configuration at that level and constructs the remaining levels around it by changing the amount of information, number of dependencies, speed, precision, dynamics, or simultaneous control required for success. A difficulty-review agent then checks each adjacent pair and rejects any spurious difficulty increase, such as requesting repeated actions or adding ambiguity. The agent also ensures that the same types of perception, memory, decisions, and control are required across difficulty levels. For example, the levels of Rotating On-Screen Keyboard (Figure 3 ) vary the code length, the number and size of keys, and the keyboard motion.
paragraphs.zh: 一个难度审查智能体首先阅读生成器、可见界面、评分器、验证器和参考求解器，以确定原始小游戏的要求。 它将该配置与一组经过批准的参考小游戏进行比较，并将其归入五个等级之一。 创作智能体保留该等级的原始配置，并通过改变成功所需的信息量、依赖关系的数量、速度、精度、动态性或同时控制要求来构建其余等级。 随后，难度审查智能体会检查每一对相邻等级，并拒绝任何虚假的难度提升，例如要求重复操作或增加歧义性。 该智能体还确保在各个难度等级上需要相同类型的感知、记忆、决策和控制。 例如，Rotating On-Screen Keyboard（图 3）的各个等级会改变代码长度、按键的数量和大小以及键盘的移动方式。

sents.en: A difficulty-review agent first reads the generator, visible interface, grader, verifier, and oracle solver to determine what the original minigame requires.
sents.zh: 一个难度审查智能体首先阅读生成器、可见界面、评分器、验证器和参考求解器，以确定原始小游戏的要求。

sents.en: It compares this configuration with an approved set of reference minigames and assigns it to one of five levels.
sents.zh: 它将该配置与一组经过批准的参考小游戏进行比较，并将其归入五个等级之一。

sents.en: The creator agent preserves the original configuration at that level and constructs the remaining levels around it by changing the amount of information, number of dependencies, speed, precision, dynamics, or simultaneous control required for success.
sents.zh: 创作智能体保留该等级的原始配置，并通过改变成功所需的信息量、依赖关系的数量、速度、精度、动态性或同时控制要求来构建其余等级。

sents.en: A difficulty-review agent then checks each adjacent pair and rejects any spurious difficulty increase, such as requesting repeated actions or adding ambiguity.
sents.zh: 随后，难度审查智能体会检查每一对相邻等级，并拒绝任何虚假的难度提升，例如要求重复操作或增加歧义性。

sents.en: The agent also ensures that the same types of perception, memory, decisions, and control are required across difficulty levels.
sents.zh: 该智能体还确保在各个难度等级上需要相同类型的感知、记忆、决策和控制。

sents.en: For example, the levels of Rotating On-Screen Keyboard (Figure 3 ) vary the code length, the number and size of keys, and the keyboard motion.
sents.zh: 例如，Rotating On-Screen Keyboard（图 3）的各个等级会改变代码长度、按键的数量和大小以及键盘的移动方式。

paragraphs.en: The creator agent also implements simplified and full interaction for every difficulty level. Simplified interaction exposes proxy controls, while full interaction requires the direct mouse or keyboard manipulation appropriate to the minigame. For example, in Rotating On-Screen Keyboard, simplified interaction lets the agent type the code directly with keyboard actions, while full interaction requires clicking the rotating keys. For a fixed seed and difficulty, the audit agent verifies that both modes generate the same minigame and differ only in the controls used to act on it. Appendices B.2 and B.3 give examples of both variations.
paragraphs.zh: 创建者智能体还为每个难度级别实现了简化交互和完整交互。 简化交互暴露代理控件，而完整交互需要与该小游戏相应的直接鼠标或键盘操作。 例如，在“旋转屏幕键盘”中，简化交互允许智能体通过键盘操作直接输入代码，而完整交互则需要点击旋转的按键。 对于固定的种子和难度，审计智能体验证两种模式生成相同的小游戏，且仅在用于对其进行操作的控制方式上有所不同。 附录 B.2 和 B.3 给出了两种变体的示例。

sents.zh: 创建者智能体还为每个难度级别实现了简化交互和完整交互。

sents.zh: 简化交互暴露代理控件，而完整交互需要与该小游戏相应的直接鼠标或键盘操作。

sents.en: For example, in Rotating On-Screen Keyboard, simplified interaction lets the agent type the code directly with keyboard actions, while full interaction requires clicking the rotating keys.
sents.zh: 例如，在“旋转屏幕键盘”中，简化交互允许智能体通过键盘操作直接输入代码，而完整交互则需要点击旋转的按键。

sents.en: For a fixed seed and difficulty, the audit agent verifies that both modes generate the same minigame and differ only in the controls used to act on it.
sents.zh: 对于固定的种子和难度，审计智能体验证两种模式生成相同的小游戏，且仅在用于对其进行操作的控制方式上有所不同。

sents.en: Appendices B.2 and B.3 give examples of both variations.
sents.zh: 附录 B.2 和 B.3 给出了两种变体的示例。

paragraphs.en: To control how much time an agent has to respond, we build an evaluation stack on top of Gym-Anything ( Aggarwal et al., 2026 ) that controls the clock of each minigame. During live execution, the task continues to change from observation through action execution at its natural speed. In Rotating On-Screen Keyboard, for example, a key can move between observation and action, so the agent must account for its position when the click executes. Since any delay between an action and its effect counts against the agent, we also build a direct connection protocol. A central server still launches and manages many sandboxes in parallel, but each agent exchanges actions and screenshots over a direct connection to its own sandbox, bypassing the server. This keeps the median time from sending an action to receiving the resulting screenshot below 50 ms in our timing tests (Appendix E.1 ). For slowed execution, the stack scales every clock of the minigame, including its timers, animations, and server-side clocks, so that a slowdown of s s advances the game by one second during s s seconds of real time. Action delivery and screenshot capture still run in real time, so the slowdown changes the time available to respond while the agent’s interaction stays the same. During paused execution, the task advances through an observation window and then freezes on the final frame until the action is executed. All settings use the same minigame, seed, difficulty, interaction mode, and verifier. Appendix E describes the evaluation protocol.
paragraphs.zh: 为了控制智能体有多少时间来响应，我们在 Gym-Anything（Aggarwal et al., 2026）之上构建了一个评估栈，用于控制每个小游戏的时钟。 在实时执行期间，任务以自然速度从观察持续变化到动作执行。 例如，在旋转屏幕键盘（Rotating On-Screen Keyboard）中，一个按键可能在观察与动作之间移动，因此智能体必须在点击执行时考虑其位置。 由于动作与其效果之间的任何延迟都会计入智能体的耗时，我们还构建了一种直接连接协议。 中央服务器仍然并行启动和管理多个沙箱，但每个智能体通过与自身沙箱的直接连接来交换动作和截图，从而绕过服务器。 在我们的计时测试中，这使得从发送动作到接收相应截图的中位时间保持在 50 毫秒以下（附录 E.1）。 对于减速执行，该栈会缩放小游戏的所有时钟，包括其计时器、动画和服务器端时钟，使得减速因子 s 使游戏在 s 秒的真实时间内推进一秒。 动作传递和截图捕捉仍以实时运行，因此减速改变的是可用来响应的时间，而智能体的交互保持不变。 在暂停执行期间，任务通过一个观察窗口推进，然后冻结在最后一帧，直到动作被执行。 所有设置使用相同的小游戏、种子、难度、交互模式和验证器。 附录 E 描述了评估协议。

paragraphs.en: To relate agent failures to the capabilities a minigame requires, a capability-review agent labels each configuration of both the real-time minigames and their counterparts for 3D visual understanding, temporal reasoning, reasoning and planning, and exploration and interface understanding (see Appendix D for definitions). It reviews the game’s program, interface, verifier, oracle solution, and recorded behavior to identify what a solution using screenshots and mouse or keyboard actions requires. Each label is supported by code or behavioral evidence. A real-time review agent checks the real-time requirement separately for each configuration, using the implementation and recorded behavior (Appendix H ).

paragraphs.en: We evaluate models by pass rate, time to solve, and inference cost, and compare these metrics across real-time minigames and their counterparts, slowdowns, difficulty levels, interaction modes, and capability requirements. Models receive task instructions and interact through screenshots, mouse actions, and keyboard input, without access to program internals or oracle solutions. Task-specific verifiers determine whether each attempt succeeds. Appendix F describes the models, prompts, budgets, and cost computation.

paragraphs.en: We evaluate Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.8-27B, GPT-6 Luna with xHigh reasoning effort, Claude Opus 5.5 with xHigh effort, and GPT-6 Astra with low and xHigh reasoning effort. We evaluate models in the live setting with full interaction at the highest difficulty, and Section 4.9 reports results on the easier difficulty levels. Following prior work on computer-use agents ( Xie et al., 2024 ; Aggarwal & Welleck, 2025 ) , models observe the environment only through screenshots and act only through mouse and keyboard actions. Models cannot run code or access the page source or program internals. In the coding experiment, we additionally allow models to run code in an isolated sandbox, where they can request screenshots and execute the same mouse and keyboard actions through an API. Interaction with the environment remains the same. Further experiments vary difficulty, interaction mode, the real-time setting, and whether interface rules are provided.

paragraphs.en: Figure 4 compares the pass rates of each model on the real-time tasks and on their non-real-time counterparts (Section 2.5 ). Even the strongest model, GPT-6 Astra (xHigh), solves only 9.0% of the real-time tasks at the highest difficulty, compared with 66.0% of their non-real-time counterparts. Interestingly, higher reasoning effort helps only when the task waits for the model: from Low to xHigh effort, Astra’s pass rate rises from 58.0% to 66.0% on the non-real-time counterparts, but only from 8.0% to 9.0% on the real-time tasks. Claude Opus 5.5 (xHigh) solves 5.0% of the real-time tasks and 57.0% of their counterparts. GPT-6 Luna (xHigh) performs worse on both, solving 1.0% of the real-time tasks and 17.0% of their counterparts, and the open-weight Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.5-9B solve only 1.0% and 0.0% of the real-time tasks. These two models also solve only 2.0% and 1.0% of the counterparts, so their failures are not specific to real time. Since each real-time task and its counterpart share the same minigame, these results show that acting in real time, rather than the underlying task, accounts for most failures of frontier models. In the following sections, we examine why.
paragraphs.zh: 图4比较了各模型在实时任务及其非实时对应任务（见2.5节）上的通过率。 即使是最强的模型 GPT-6 Astra（xHigh），在最高难度下也只能解决9.0%的实时任务，而其非实时对应任务的通过率为66.0%。 有趣的是，更高的推理努力只有在任务等待模型时才有帮助：从Low到xHigh努力程度，Astra在非实时对应任务上的通过率从58.0%上升到66.0%，但在实时任务上仅从8.0%上升到9.0%。 Claude Opus 5.5（xHigh）解决了5.0%的实时任务和57.0%的对应任务。 GPT-6 Luna（xHigh）在两者上的表现都更差，仅解决了1.0%的实时任务和17.0%的对应任务，而开源权重模型 Qwen3.8-27B 和 Qwen3.5-9B 仅解决了1.0%和0.0%的实时任务。 这两个模型在对应任务上也仅解决了2.0%和1.0%，因此它们的失败并非实时性所特有。 由于每个实时任务与其对应任务共享相同的小游戏，这些结果表明，是实时行动而非底层任务本身，造成了前沿模型的大部分失败。 在接下来的章节中，我们将探究其原因。

paragraphs.en: To study how response speed limits performance, we use our evaluation stack to slow down the environment while leaving the model’s inference unchanged (Section 2.5 ). A slowdown of s s advances the environment clock at 1 / s 1/s of its normal rate, giving the model more time to respond before the task changes, while pausing freezes the environment until the model acts. Figure 5 reports the pass rate of GPT-6 Astra on the same 100 real-time tasks at the highest difficulty as we slow the environment. With xHigh reasoning effort, pass rate rises steadily from 9% at normal speed to 17% at 4 × 4\times , 48% at 16 × 16\times , and 57% at 64 × 64\times slowdown, and reaches 75% when the environment is paused. Pausing similarly raises GPT-6 Luna’s pass rate on real-time tasks from 6.0% to 29.8% across all difficulty levels. Since the tasks are unchanged and only the time available to respond grows, these results show that for frontier models, slow responses are the primary reason for failure in real time.
paragraphs.zh: 为了研究响应速度如何限制性能，我们使用评估栈在保持模型推理不变的情况下减慢环境（见第 2.5 节）。 减慢 s 倍使环境时钟以正常速率的 1/s 前进，让模型在任务变化之前有更多时间响应，而暂停则会冻结环境，直到智能体采取行动。 图 5 报告了在最高难度下，随着环境被减慢，GPT-6 Astra 在相同的 100 个实时任务上的通过率。 在 xHigh 推理努力下，通过率从正常速度下的 9% 稳步上升到减慢 4 倍时的 17%、16 倍时的 48%、64 倍时的 57%，而在环境暂停时达到 75%。 暂停同样使 GPT-6 Luna 在所有难度级别的实时任务上的通过率从 6.0% 提高到 29.8%。 由于任务本身不变，只是可用于响应的时间增加了，这些结果表明，对于前沿模型而言，响应缓慢是其在实时场景中失败的主要原因。

paragraphs.en: Moreover, the benefit of additional time grows with reasoning effort. At normal speed, Low and xHigh effort perform similarly, 8% and 9%, since additional reasoning also takes additional time. As the environment slows, xHigh pulls ahead, reaching 57% at 64 × 64\times compared with 42% for Low, and 75% compared with 58% when paused. Interestingly, even at 64 × 64\times slowdown, Astra (xHigh) remains 18 points below its paused performance, suggesting that some tasks remain difficult as long as the environment keeps changing at all.
paragraphs.zh: 此外，额外时间带来的收益会随着推理力度而增长。 在正常速度下，Low 与 xHigh 力度的表现相近，分别为 8% 和 9%，因为额外的推理也会耗费额外的时间。 随着环境变慢，xHigh 逐渐领先，在 64 × 64 倍减速时达到 57%，而 Low 为 42%；在暂停状态下则分别为 75% 和 58%。 有趣的是，即使处于 64 × 64 倍减速环境，Astra（xHigh）仍比其暂停状态下的表现低 18 个百分点，这表明只要环境仍在持续变化，某些任务就依然困难。

paragraphs.en: Since frontier models are strong coding agents, we next examine whether they can use code to compensate for their slow responses. We allow models to run code in an isolated sandbox, where they can request screenshots and execute the same mouse and keyboard actions through an API (Appendix F.5 ). The action space is unchanged, but models can now write scripts that observe and act without waiting for the model’s next response. Table 3 reports results at the highest difficulty with full interaction in the live setting. Coding raises the pass rate of Astra (xHigh) on real-time tasks from 9.0% to 31.0%, a 3.4-fold increase, compared with a gain of only 8.0 points on their non-real-time counterparts, from 66.0% to 74.0%. The gain also grows with model capability: Astra (Low) improves from 8.0% to 14.0%, and Luna only from 1.0% to 5.0%.
paragraphs.zh: 由于前沿模型是强大的编码智能体，我们接下来考察它们能否利用代码来弥补其响应缓慢的问题。 我们允许智能体在隔离的沙箱中运行代码，在那里它们可以通过 API 请求截图并执行相同的鼠标和键盘操作（附录 F.5）。 动作空间保持不变，但智能体现在可以编写脚本，在无需等待智能体下一次响应的情况下进行观察和操作。 表 3 报告了在实时环境下以完全交互方式在最高难度下的结果。 编码将 Astra（xHigh）在实时任务上的通过率从 9.0% 提升到 31.0%，提高了 3.4 倍，相比之下，在对应的非实时任务上仅提升了 8.0 个百分点，从 66.0% 提升到 74.0%。 这一提升还随智能体能力的增强而增长：Astra（Low）从 8.0% 提升到 14.0%，而 Luna 仅从 1.0% 提升到 5.0%。

sents.en: Since frontier models are strong coding agents, we next examine whether they can use code to compensate for their slow responses.
sents.zh: 由于前沿模型是强大的编码智能体，我们接下来考察它们能否利用代码来弥补其响应缓慢的问题。

sents.en: We allow models to run code in an isolated sandbox, where they can request screenshots and execute the same mouse and keyboard actions through an API (Appendix F.5 ).

sents.en: The action space is unchanged, but models can now write scripts that observe and act without waiting for the model’s next response.
sents.zh: 动作空间保持不变，但智能体现在可以编写脚本，在无需等待智能体下一次响应的情况下进行观察和操作。

sents.en: Table 3 reports results at the highest difficulty with full interaction in the live setting.
sents.zh: 表 3 报告了在实时环境下以完全交互方式在最高难度下的结果。

sents.en: Coding raises the pass rate of Astra (xHigh) on real-time tasks from 9.0% to 31.0%, a 3.4-fold increase, compared with a gain of only 8.0 points on their non-real-time counterparts, from 66.0% to 74.0%.
sents.zh: 编码将 Astra（xHigh）在实时任务上的通过率从 9.0% 提升到 31.0%，提高了 3.4 倍，相比之下，在对应的非实时任务上仅提升了 8.0 个百分点，从 66.0% 提升到 74.0%。

sents.en: The gain also grows with model capability: Astra (Low) improves from 8.0% to 14.0%, and Luna only from 1.0% to 5.0%.
sents.zh: 这一提升还随智能体能力的增强而增长：Astra（Low）从 8.0% 提升到 14.0%，而 Luna 仅从 1.0% 提升到 5.0%。

paragraphs.en: To understand this gain, we inspect Astra’s trajectories. Astra writes image-processing scripts that perceive and act between its own responses. For instance, in Rotating On-Screen Keyboard, it locates the moving keys using image template matching and clicks them within 200 ms. In Clockwork Clutch Safe, where moving gears must be aligned, it tracks gear markers and times clutch releases using estimates of their motion (Appendix G ). In effect, the model moves the real-time part of the task into code, and reasons only about what the code should do. This suggests that similar scripts could help slow models act in other real-time domains, such as video games and physical interfaces. Nonetheless, coding still leaves Astra far below its paused performance of 75.0%, and such scripts are difficult to write when the relevant visual information cannot be extracted reliably or prepared for in advance.
paragraphs.zh: 为了理解这一提升，我们检视 Astra 的轨迹。 Astra 编写图像处理脚本，使其能在自己的两次响应之间进行感知和行动。 例如，在 Rotating On-Screen Keyboard 任务中，它使用图像模板匹配来定位移动的按键，并在 200 毫秒内点击它们。 在 Clockwork Clutch Safe 任务中，需要将移动的齿轮对齐，它会跟踪齿轮标记，并利用对其运动的估计来把握离合器释放的时机（附录 G）。 实际上，该模型将任务的实时部分转移到了代码中，只对代码应当做什么进行推理。 这表明，类似的脚本可以帮助较慢的模型在其他实时领域（如视频游戏和物理界面）中行动。 尽管如此，编写代码仍使 Astra 远低于其暂停状态下的 75.0% 表现，而且当相关视觉信息无法可靠提取或提前准备时，这类脚本很难编写。

paragraphs.en: Real-time applications require agents that are not only accurate, but also fast and affordable. Table 3 reports the pass rate, average time, and average inference cost per attempt on the 100 real-time tasks at the highest difficulty. Astra (xHigh) achieves the highest pass rate, 9.0%, but takes 7.2 minutes and costs $4.50 per attempt on average. Lowering its reasoning effort to Low reduces the time to 4.3 minutes and the cost to $2.76, with a similar pass rate of 8.0%, consistent with additional reasoning helping little when the environment does not wait. Claude Opus 5.5 (xHigh) costs the most, $6.40 per attempt, and takes 15.8 minutes, while solving only 5.0% of the tasks. Luna is far cheaper at $0.07 per attempt, but takes 6.4 minutes and solves only 1.0% of the tasks. Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.5-9B cost $0.64 and $0.62 per attempt, but take about ten times longer than Luna, 63.0 and 75.9 minutes, while solving only 1.0% and 0.0% of the tasks. As a case study, we compare these results with those of a human author who, like the evaluated models, sees each minigame for the first time. On 20 randomly sampled tasks, the human solves 9 tasks, or 45.0%, in an average of 2.2 minutes per task (Appendix F.7 ). This is five times the pass rate of Astra (xHigh), in less than a third of its average time. These results show that progress in real-time interaction requires improving not only the pass rate of models, but also their speed and cost ( Abhyankar et al., 2026 ; Black et al., 2025 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 实时应用要求智能体不仅准确，而且快速且经济。 表3报告了在最高难度的100个实时任务上的通过率、平均耗时和每次尝试的平均推理成本。 Astra (xHigh) 取得了最高的通过率9.0%，但平均每次尝试需要7.2分钟并花费4.50美元。 将其推理力度降至Low可将时间缩短至4.3分钟、成本降至2.76美元，同时保持相近的8.0%通过率，这与以下观察一致：当环境不等人时，额外的推理帮助甚微。 Claude Opus 5.5 (xHigh) 成本最高，每次尝试6.40美元，耗时15.8分钟，却只解决了5.0%的任务。 Luna便宜得多，每次尝试仅需0.07美元，但需要6.4分钟且只解决了1.0%的任务。 Qwen3.8-27B和Qwen3.5-9B每次尝试分别花费0.64美元和0.62美元，但耗时约为Luna的十倍，分别为63.0分钟和75.9分钟，且只解决了1.0%和0.0%的任务。 作为案例研究，我们将这些结果与一位人类作者的结果进行比较，该作者与被评估的模型一样，都是首次接触每个小游戏。 在随机抽取的20个任务中，人类解决了9个任务，即45.0%，平均每个任务耗时2.2分钟（附录F.7）。 这是Astra (xHigh) 通过率的五倍，而平均用时不到其三分之一。 这些结果表明，实时交互方面的进展不仅需要提高模型的通过率，还需要提升其速度并降低其成本（Abhyankar et al., 2026；Black et al., 2025）。

paragraphs.en: Besides response speed, our controls let us study which other capabilities limit agents. We first examine whether the benefit of pausing is limited to real-time tasks. Figure 6 compares live and paused execution for GPT-6 Luna with full interaction, averaged across all five difficulty levels. Interestingly, pausing also helps on the non-real-time counterparts that require temporal reasoning, raising Luna’s pass rate from 20.4% to 31.4%, while the gain on counterparts without temporal reasoning, from 45.2% to 52.7%, is not statistically significant ( p = 0.443 p=0.443 ). Since these counterparts do not require acting in real time, this suggests that models also struggle to reason about scenes that change over time, even when they need not act quickly, identifying temporal reasoning as a further source of difficulty. Moreover, even when paused, Luna solves only 29.8% of the real-time tasks, showing that for weaker models, response speed is only one of several bottlenecks.
paragraphs.zh: 除了响应速度之外，我们的控制手段还让我们能够研究还有哪些能力会限制智能体。 我们首先考察暂停所带来的收益是否仅限于实时任务。 图 6 比较了 GPT-6 Luna 在完全交互模式下实时执行与暂停执行的表现，结果是在全部五个难度等级上取平均。 有趣的是，暂停在需要时间推理的非实时对应任务上同样有帮助，将 Luna 的通过率从 20.4% 提升到 31.4%，而在不需要时间推理的对应任务上，从 45.2% 到 52.7% 的提升则不具有统计显著性（ p = 0.443 p=0.443 ）。 由于这些对应任务不需要实时行动，这表明模型在推理随时间变化的场景时也会遇到困难，即使它们无需快速行动，这说明时间推理是另一个困难来源。 此外，即使在暂停模式下，Luna 也只能解决 29.8% 的实时任务，这表明对于较弱的模型而言，响应速度只是诸多瓶颈之一。

paragraphs.en: Since review agents label the capabilities each configuration requires, we can also relate performance to the demands of a task. Figure 9 reports Luna’s pass rate as a function of the number of required capabilities, using full interaction across all five difficulty levels. In the live setting, pass rate decreases from 37.0% when one capability is required to 7.2% when all four are required, and paused execution shows the same trend, from 55.6% to 23.2%. Since the decline persists when the environment is paused, tasks become harder as capabilities are combined, even without time pressure. However, since capability requirements overlap across tasks, this analysis cannot isolate the effect of a single capability. We therefore examine interface exploration directly through a controlled experiment in Section 4.8 .
paragraphs.zh: 由于审阅智能体会标注每个配置所需的能力，我们还可以将性能与任务的需求关联起来。 图 9 报告了 Luna 的通过率随所需能力数量变化的函数关系，实验在全部五个难度级别上采用完整交互。 在实时设置中，当需要一项能力时通过率为 37.0%，当需要全部四项能力时降至 7.2%；暂停执行也呈现相同趋势，从 55.6% 降至 23.2%。 由于在环境暂停时这一下降依然存在，说明即使没有时间压力，随着能力的组合，任务也变得更难。 然而，由于各任务之间的能力需求存在重叠，该分析无法隔离单一能力的影响。 因此，我们在 4.8 节中通过一个受控实验直接考察界面探索。

sents.en: We therefore examine interface exploration directly through a controlled experiment in Section 4.8 .
sents.zh: 因此，我们在 4.8 节中通过一个受控实验直接考察界面探索。

paragraphs.en: Many minigames require the agent to learn how an unfamiliar interface behaves before it can solve the task. To isolate this demand, we append an environment-specific rulebook describing the controls, action effects, and world rules to Luna’s task prompt (Appendix F.6 ), and evaluate with full interaction in the live setting on minigames requiring exploration and interface understanding. Figure 9 shows that providing these rules raises Luna’s pass rate from 11.3% to 16.2% across the five difficulty levels. The model must still solve the same minigame and carry out its solution through the same controls, so this gain comes from knowing the rules in advance. This identifies interface exploration as a further source of difficulty: Luna can use interface knowledge that it struggles to acquire through interaction.
paragraphs.zh: 许多小游戏要求智能体先学会一个陌生界面的运作方式，才能完成该任务。 为了分离出这一需求，我们在 Luna 的任务提示中附加一份描述操作方式、动作效果和世界规则的环境专属规则手册（附录 F.6），并在需要探索和界面理解的小游戏上以实时环境中的完整交互进行评估。 图 9 显示，提供这些规则使 Luna 在五个难度级别上的通过率从 11.3% 提升至 16.2%。 模型仍需解决同样的小游戏，并通过同样的操作执行其解法，因此这一提升来自提前知晓规则。 这表明界面探索是另一个难度来源：Luna 能够利用那些它难以通过交互获取的界面知识。

paragraphs.en: Finally, we turn to the easier difficulty levels and simplified interaction. Table 4 reports Luna’s pass rates in the live setting with full interaction across all five difficulty levels. While Luna solves only 1.0% of the real-time tasks at the highest difficulty, it solves 15.0% at difficulty 1, so the easier levels leave room to measure progress for weaker models. On their non-real-time counterparts, its pass rate falls from 35.0% to 17.0%. The gap between the two stays between 14.0 and 27.0 points at every difficulty, so acting in real time is a major source of failure even on the easiest tasks. To study difficulty without this effect, Figure 9 reports Luna’s pass rate on real-time tasks across the five difficulty levels under paused execution. Averaged across both interaction modes, pass rate decreases from 53.0% at difficulty 1 to 15.5% at difficulty 5, showing that the difficulty levels provide a controlled range of challenge. Simplified interaction raises the overall pass rate from 29.8% to 33.2%, with larger gains at higher difficulty. Since both modes realize the same minigame, this gain shows that some failures arise from operating the full controls rather than from solving the task. However, the decline with difficulty persists under simplified interaction, showing that the challenges introduced at higher difficulty levels are not only about the controls.

paragraphs.en: Real-time interaction. Acting in a changing environment requires accounting for the delay between observing it and acting on it. Robotics methods handle this delay through asynchronous execution or by predicting the state at execution time ( Black et al., 2025 ; Shukor et al., 2025 ; Tang et al., 2025 ) , and reinforcement learning studies decision making under action and observation delays ( Ramstedt & Pal, 2019 ; Derman et al., 2021 ) . For computer-use agents, OSWorld-Human measures latency and finds that agents take 2.7 to 4.3 times more steps than necessary ( Abhyankar et al., 2026 ) . Game benchmarks either pause the game during inference ( Ouyang et al., 2026 ) or compare paused and real-time play ( Zhang et al., 2026 ; Park et al., 2025 ) , and Real-Time Reasoning Gym adds time pressure to text-based games ( Wen et al., 2026 ) . However, these comparisons cover only a few visual games or text-based environments. Gym-Anything-RT pairs each of 100 real-time minigames with a non-real-time counterpart and controls the clock of each minigame, so that we can vary how much time an agent has to respond on the same task.
paragraphs.zh: 实时交互。 在不断变化的环境中行动，需要考虑观察环境与对环境采取行动之间的延迟。 机器人学方法通过异步执行或预测执行时刻的状态来处理这种延迟（ Black et al., 2025 ; Shukor et al., 2025 ; Tang et al., 2025 ），而强化学习则研究在动作延迟和观察延迟下的决策问题（ Ramstedt & Pal, 2019 ; Derman et al., 2021 ）。 对于计算机使用的智能体，OSWorld-Human 测量了延迟，发现智能体采取的步骤是必要步骤的 2.7 到 4.3 倍（ Abhyankar et al., 2026 ）。 游戏基准要么在推理期间暂停游戏（ Ouyang et al., 2026 ），要么比较暂停模式与实时模式下的表现（ Zhang et al., 2026 ; Park et al., 2025 ），而 Real-Time Reasoning Gym 则为文本游戏增加了时间压力（ Wen et al., 2026 ）。 然而，这些比较仅涵盖少数视觉游戏或基于文本的环境。 Gym-Anything-RT 将 100 个实时小游戏分别与非实时对应版本配对，并控制每个小游戏的时钟，从而让我们能够在同一任务上改变智能体可用于响应的时间。

paragraphs.en: Benchmarks for interactive visual agents. Benchmarks for vision-language agents cover websites ( Zhou et al., 2024 ; Koh et al., 2024 ) , desktop and mobile applications ( Xie et al., 2024 ; Bonatti et al., 2024 ; Yuan et al., 2026 ; Rawles et al., 2024 ) , professional software ( Aggarwal & Welleck, 2025 ; Aggarwal et al., 2026 ) , games ( Zhang et al., 2026 ; Paglieri et al., 2025 ; Hu et al., 2025a ; Zheng et al., 2025a ; Ying et al., 2026 ; Ouyang et al., 2026 ; ARC Prize Foundation, 2026 ) , and embodied simulators ( Savva et al., 2019 ; Shridhar et al., 2020 ; Srivastava et al., 2021 ; Yang et al., 2025c ) . However, most of these environments wait for the agent between actions, and each task requires many capabilities at once, so low performance does not reveal which capability limits the agent. Prior works address the latter by mapping tasks to capabilities ( Wu et al., 2023 ) , evaluating perception, reasoning, and decision making separately ( Wang et al., 2025c ; Xu et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2024 ) , or varying one condition of a task, such as difficulty, the initial state, or the interface ( Davydova et al., 2025 ; Zheng et al., 2025b ; Zhao et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2026 ) . Gym-Anything-RT instead varies the real-time requirement, difficulty, and interaction interface of the same minigame.
paragraphs.zh: 面向交互式视觉智能体的基准测试。 面向视觉-语言智能体的基准测试覆盖了网站（Zhou 等，2024；Koh 等，2024）、桌面与移动应用（Xie 等，2024；Bonatti 等，2024；Yuan 等，2026；Rawles 等，2024）、专业软件（Aggarwal & Welleck，2025；Aggarwal 等，2026）、游戏（Zhang 等，2026；Paglieri 等，2025；Hu 等，2025a；Zheng 等，2025a；Ying 等，2026；Ouyang 等，2026；ARC Prize Foundation，2026）以及具身模拟器（Savva 等，2019；Shridhar 等，2020；Srivastava 等，2021；Yang 等，2025c）。 然而，这些环境大多在动作之间等待智能体，且每个任务同时需要多种能力，因此低性能无法揭示究竟是哪种能力限制了智能体。 已有工作通过将任务映射到能力（Wu 等，2023）、分别评估感知、推理与决策（Wang 等，2025c；Xu 等，2026；Li 等，2024），或改变任务的某一条件，例如难度、初始状态或界面（Davydova 等，2025；Zheng 等，2025b；Zhao 等，2025；Liu 等，2026），来解决后者问题。 Gym-Anything-RT 则改变同一小游戏中的实时性要求、难度和交互界面。

paragraphs.en: Capability-specific evaluation of VLMs. Many benchmarks test individual capabilities of VLMs through questions about images or videos, such as 3D spatial understanding ( Yang et al., 2025a ; Wang et al., 2025b ; Ma et al., 2024 ; Jia et al., 2025 ) , temporal reasoning ( Liu et al., 2024 ; Shangguan et al., 2024 ; Zhang et al., 2024 ) , GUI grounding ( Cheng et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2025 ) , and abstract reasoning ( Chia et al., 2024 ; Ghosal et al., 2024 ; Song et al., 2025 ) . However, the model answers a question about a fixed input, without acting on what it perceives. iVISPAR and VisGym evaluate visual reasoning through interaction ( Mayer et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2026b ) . Gym-Anything-RT further requires agents to perceive and act while the minigame keeps changing.
paragraphs.zh: 针对视觉语言模型（VLM）特定能力的评测。 许多基准通过关于图像或视频的问题来测试视觉语言模型（VLM）的单项能力，例如 3D 空间理解（Yang et al., 2025a; Wang et al., 2025b; Ma et al., 2024; Jia et al., 2025）、时序推理（Liu et al., 2024; Shangguan et al., 2024; Zhang et al., 2024）、GUI 定位（Cheng et al., 2024; Li et al., 2025）以及抽象推理（Chia et al., 2024; Ghosal et al., 2024; Song et al., 2025）。 然而，模型只是针对固定的输入回答问题，并不根据其感知到的内容采取行动。iVISPAR 和 VisGym 则通过交互来评测视觉推理（Mayer et al., 2025; Wang et al., 2026b）。 Gym-Anything-RT 进一步要求智能体在小游戏不断变化的情况下进行感知和行动。

paragraphs.en: Automated environment construction. Recent works use coding agents and LLMs to construct computer-use environments ( Aggarwal et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2026a ; Cao et al., 2026 ) , text-based environments ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) , and environments with tasks of varying difficulty ( Hu et al., 2025b ; Faldor et al., 2024 ) , while procedural generators vary the complexity of task instances ( Cobbe et al., 2019 ; Samvelyan et al., 2021 ; Chevalier-Boisvert et al., 2019 ; Stojanovski et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2025 ) . However, none of these produce visual minigames whose timing, difficulty, and interaction interface can be varied while preserving the underlying task. We extend the creator and audit agents of Gym-Anything ( Aggarwal et al., 2026 ) to construct such minigames, each with a non-real-time counterpart and an oracle solution. Appendix I provides a more detailed related work.
paragraphs.zh: 自动化环境构建。 近期的工作使用编码智能体和大语言模型来构建计算机使用环境（Aggarwal et al., 2026；Wang et al., 2026a；Cao et al., 2026）、基于文本的环境（Zhang et al., 2025）以及包含不同难度任务的环境（Hu et al., 2025b；Faldor et al., 2024），同时程序化生成器用于改变任务实例的复杂度（Cobbe et al., 2019；Samvelyan et al., 2021；Chevalier-Boisvert et al., 2019；Stojanovski et al., 2025；Chen et al., 2025）。 然而，这些工作都无法生成视觉小游戏，这类小游戏可以在保留底层任务的前提下改变其时间控制、难度和交互界面。 我们扩展了 Gym-Anything（Aggarwal et al., 2026）中的创建者智能体和审计智能体来构建此类小游戏，每个小游戏都有一个非实时的对应版本和一个最优解。 附录 I 提供了更详细的 related work（相关工作）。

paragraphs.en: In this work, we introduced Gym-Anything-RT , a scalable framework for creating environments for studying the real-time interaction capabilities of vision-language agents. In Gym-Anything-RT , coding agents implement and audit each environment as a visual minigame program with an oracle solution, and our evaluation stack controls the clock of each minigame. As a result, we can vary how much time an agent has to respond, whether the task requires real-time interaction, its difficulty, and its interaction interface on the same minigame. Using Gym-Anything-RT , we constructed a benchmark of 100 real-time minigames and showed that current agents perform poorly in real time, with the strongest agent, GPT-6 Astra (xHigh), solving only 9.0% of the real-time tasks compared with 66.0% of their non-real-time counterparts. We further showed that speed is the primary bottleneck for frontier models, and that temporal reasoning and exploration of unfamiliar interfaces are additional sources of difficulty. Interestingly, we also find that frontier agents can partially offset their poor real-time capabilities by writing code that perceives and acts on their behalf.
paragraphs.zh: 在本工作中，我们提出了 Gym-Anything-RT，一个用于创建环境的可扩展框架，用以研究视觉-语言智能体的实时交互能力。 在 Gym-Anything-RT 中，编程智能体将每个环境实现为带有标准答案程序的视觉小游戏并进行审计，我们的评估栈控制每个小游戏的时钟。 因此，我们可以在同一个小游戏上改变智能体可用的响应时间、任务是否需要实时交互、任务难度以及交互界面。 利用 Gym-Anything-RT，我们构建了一个包含 100 个实时小游戏的基准测试，并表明当前智能体在实时场景下表现不佳：最强的智能体 GPT-6 Astra (xHigh) 仅解决了 9.0% 的实时任务，而其非实时对应任务的解决率为 66.0%。 我们进一步表明，速度是前沿模型的主要瓶颈，而时序推理和对陌生界面的探索则是额外的难度来源。 有趣的是，我们还发现前沿智能体可以通过编写代码来代替自身进行感知和行动，从而部分弥补其实时能力的不足。

sents.en: In this work, we introduced Gym-Anything-RT , a scalable framework for creating environments for studying the real-time interaction capabilities of vision-language agents.
sents.zh: 在本工作中，我们提出了 Gym-Anything-RT，一个用于创建环境的可扩展框架，用以研究视觉-语言智能体的实时交互能力。

sents.en: In Gym-Anything-RT , coding agents implement and audit each environment as a visual minigame program with an oracle solution, and our evaluation stack controls the clock of each minigame.
sents.zh: 在 Gym-Anything-RT 中，编程智能体将每个环境实现为带有标准答案程序的视觉小游戏并进行审计，我们的评估栈控制每个小游戏的时钟。

sents.en: As a result, we can vary how much time an agent has to respond, whether the task requires real-time interaction, its difficulty, and its interaction interface on the same minigame.
sents.zh: 因此，我们可以在同一个小游戏上改变智能体可用的响应时间、任务是否需要实时交互、任务难度以及交互界面。

sents.en: Using Gym-Anything-RT , we constructed a benchmark of 100 real-time minigames and showed that current agents perform poorly in real time, with the strongest agent, GPT-6 Astra (xHigh), solving only 9.0% of the real-time tasks compared with 66.0% of their non-real-time counterparts.
sents.zh: 利用 Gym-Anything-RT，我们构建了一个包含 100 个实时小游戏的基准测试，并表明当前智能体在实时场景下表现不佳：最强的智能体 GPT-6 Astra (xHigh) 仅解决了 9.0% 的实时任务，而其非实时对应任务的解决率为 66.0%。

sents.en: We further showed that speed is the primary bottleneck for frontier models, and that temporal reasoning and exploration of unfamiliar interfaces are additional sources of difficulty.
sents.zh: 我们进一步表明，速度是前沿模型的主要瓶颈，而时序推理和对陌生界面的探索则是额外的难度来源。

sents.en: Interestingly, we also find that frontier agents can partially offset their poor real-time capabilities by writing code that perceives and acts on their behalf.
sents.zh: 有趣的是，我们还发现前沿智能体可以通过编写代码来代替自身进行感知和行动，从而部分弥补其实时能力的不足。

paragraphs.en: More broadly, our results suggest that progress in real-time interaction requires agents that are not only capable but also fast. We hope that Gym-Anything-RT and the released minigames provide a foundation for future work on real-time agents, including faster models, agents that move the time-critical parts of a task into code, and training on real-time environments.
paragraphs.zh: 更广泛地说，我们的结果表明，实时交互的进步需要不仅能力强而且速度快的智能体。 我们希望 Gym-Anything-RT 和发布的迷你游戏能为未来实时智能体方面的研究奠定基础，包括更快的模型、将任务中时间关键部分转移到代码中的智能体，以及在实时环境中的训练。

sents.en: More broadly, our results suggest that progress in real-time interaction requires agents that are not only capable but also fast.
sents.zh: 更广泛地说，我们的结果表明，实时交互的进步需要不仅能力强而且速度快的智能体。

sents.en: We hope that Gym-Anything-RT and the released minigames provide a foundation for future work on real-time agents, including faster models, agents that move the time-critical parts of a task into code, and training on real-time environments.
sents.zh: 我们希望 Gym-Anything-RT 和发布的迷你游戏能为未来实时智能体方面的研究奠定基础，包括更快的模型、将任务中时间关键部分转移到代码中的智能体，以及在实时环境中的训练。

paragraphs.en: We focus on evaluating existing agents, although our programmatic task generators and automatic verifiers also provide a basis for training. Studying whether training on these minigames improves real-time interaction is an important direction for future work.
paragraphs.zh: 我们专注于评估现有的智能体，不过我们的程序化任务生成器和自动验证器也为训练提供了基础。 研究在这些小游戏上进行训练能否提升实时交互能力，是未来工作的一个重要方向。

sents.zh: 我们专注于评估现有的智能体，不过我们的程序化任务生成器和自动验证器也为训练提供了基础。

sents.en: Studying whether training on these minigames improves real-time interaction is an important direction for future work.
sents.zh: 研究在这些小游戏上进行训练能否提升实时交互能力，是未来工作的一个重要方向。

paragraphs.en: Our minigames capture specific demands of real-time environments to enable controlled comparisons across capabilities, difficulty, and interaction. Whether improvements on these tasks transfer to complete games and physical interfaces remains an open question.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的迷你游戏捕捉了实时环境的特定需求，以便在能力、难度和交互之间进行可控的比较。 在这些任务上的改进能否迁移到完整的游戏和物理界面上，仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。

paragraphs.en: Finally, Gym-Anything-RT covers a selected set of capabilities and task mechanics. Our creation–audit framework provides a way to extend this coverage with additional minigames and capability combinations.
paragraphs.zh: 最后，Gym-Anything-RT 涵盖了一组精选的能力与任务机制。 我们的创建–审计框架提供了一种通过额外的迷你游戏和能力组合来扩展这一覆盖范围的方式。

paragraphs.en: This appendix details the construction procedure summarized in Section 2 . All agents in the construction pipeline use GPT-6 Astra.
paragraphs.zh: 本附录详细介绍了第 2 节中总结的构建流程。 构建流水线中的所有智能体均使用 GPT-6 Astra。

sents.en: This appendix details the construction procedure summarized in Section 2 .
sents.zh: 本附录详细介绍了第 2 节中总结的构建流程。

sents.en: All agents in the construction pipeline use GPT-6 Astra.
sents.zh: 构建流水线中的所有智能体均使用 GPT-6 Astra。

paragraphs.en: The creator agent receives one selected minigame together with its survey records and source links. It also inspects previously approved minigames as working examples of the environment structure. The creator implements the environment specification, task, generator, browser interface, server grader, exported verifier, oracle solver, difficulty and interaction controls, real-time settings, and tests. It may create or edit only the files of its own minigame and cannot modify the shared runtime, evaluator, or clock. The creator runs all ten difficulty and interaction configurations in the browser in the live and paused settings and checks generation, grading, result export, verification, failure, and retry. It records screenshots, recordings, and command outputs as evidence, together with a solution video in which the oracle solver completes the task in the browser.
paragraphs.zh: 创建者智能体接收一个被选中的小游戏，连同其问卷记录和来源链接。 它还会查看之前已批准的小游戏，作为环境结构的工作示例。 创建者实现环境规范、任务、生成器、浏览器界面、服务器评分器、导出的验证器、神谕求解器、难度和交互控制、实时设置以及测试。 它只能创建或编辑自己小游戏内的文件，不能修改共享的运行时、评估器或时钟。 创建者在浏览器中以实时和暂停设置运行全部十种难度和交互配置，并检查生成、评分、结果导出、验证、失败和重试。 它记录截图、录像和命令输出作为证据，同时提供一段神谕求解器在浏览器中完成任务的解决方案视频。

paragraphs.en: A fresh audit agent then inspects the environment and its evidence without modifying any files. It checks the following items and ends its report with a verdict of PASS or REVISION_REQUIRED .
paragraphs.zh: 随后一个全新的审计智能体在不修改任何文件的情况下检查环境及其证据。 它检查以下各项，并在报告结尾给出 PASS 或 REVISION_REQUIRED 的判定。

paragraphs.en: Difficulty baseline. The generated task is assigned to the appropriate level by comparison with approved reference minigames, without relying on the environment name or the creator’s description.
paragraphs.zh: 难度基准。 通过与已审核的参考小游戏进行比较，将生成的任务分配到适当的等级，而不依赖环境名称或创建者的描述。

paragraphs.en: Difficulty variations. Levels 1 to 5 increase in what the agent must perceive, decide, remember, or control. Adding repetitive steps is not sufficient.

paragraphs.en: Interaction. For the same seed and difficulty, simplified and full interaction use the same minigame, information, goal, timing, physics, tolerances, and success condition. Full interaction requires the intended mouse or keyboard operations on the minigame.

paragraphs.en: Real time. In live execution, the environment continues while the model produces an action. In paused execution, it remains frozen until the action arrives, and the action then executes with the intended behavior. The real-time configurations satisfy the definition in Appendix H , and no mechanism lets the agent avoid acting in real time, such as a brake that halts moving parts or repeating motion that permits a precomputed solution.
paragraphs.zh: 实时。 在实时执行中，环境在模型产生动作的同时持续运行。 在暂停执行中，环境保持冻结，直到动作到达，随后该动作以预期行为执行。 实时配置满足附录 H 中的定义，且没有任何机制能让智能体回避实时行动，例如能让运动部件停止的制动器，或允许使用预先计算好的解决方案的重复运动。

paragraphs.en: The five difficulty levels, from very easy (level 1) to very hard (level 5), are defined in the same way for every minigame in Gym-Anything-RT . A level describes the exact configuration the agent receives, and the original configuration of a minigame can belong to any level. A difficulty-review agent assigns levels by comparison with approved reference minigames, including Isometric Voxel Extraction Mine (level 1), Cursor-Controlled Constellation Hunt (level 2), Gyroscopic Tilt Board (level 3), Blind Dice Courier (level 4), and Exact-Change Candy Cascade (level 5).
paragraphs.zh: 五个难度等级，从非常简单（等级 1）到非常困难（等级 5），在 Gym-Anything-RT 中的每个小游戏里都以相同的方式定义。 等级描述智能体所获得的确切配置，而一个小游戏的原始配置可以属于任意等级。 难度审查智能体通过与已批准的参考小游戏进行比较来分配等级，这些参考小游戏包括等距体素提取矿场（等级 1）、光标控制星座搜寻（等级 2）、陀螺倾斜板（等级 3）、盲骰快递员（等级 4）和精确找零糖果瀑布（等级 5）。

sents.zh: 五个难度等级，从非常简单（等级 1）到非常困难（等级 5），在 Gym-Anything-RT 中的每个小游戏里都以相同的方式定义。

sents.zh: 难度审查智能体通过与已批准的参考小游戏进行比较来分配等级，这些参考小游戏包括等距体素提取矿场（等级 1）、光标控制星座搜寻（等级 2）、陀螺倾斜板（等级 3）、盲骰快递员（等级 4）和精确找零糖果瀑布（等级 5）。

paragraphs.en: To construct the other levels, the creator changes parameters that alter the problem the agent must solve. Depending on the minigame, these include the information available to the agent, visual ambiguity, the number of variables handled together, dependencies between decisions, planning depth, motion speed and timing windows, action precision, and recovery options. More steps, rounds, or waiting do not by themselves make a configuration harder. For every pair of adjacent levels, the creator must state what changes in the agent’s decision or control problem. Table 5 shows the five levels of Rotating On-Screen Keyboard.
paragraphs.zh: 为了构建其他关卡，创建者通过改变参数来改变智能体需要解决的问题。 根据小游戏的不同，这些参数包括智能体可获得的信息、视觉模糊性、同时处理的变量数量、决策之间的依赖关系、规划深度、运动速度和时机窗口、操作精度以及恢复选项。 更多的步骤、回合或等待本身并不会使配置变得更难。 对于每一对相邻关卡，创建者必须说明智能体的决策或控制问题发生了什么变化。 表 5 展示了「旋转屏幕键盘」的五个关卡。

sents.zh: 为了构建其他关卡，创建者通过改变参数来改变智能体需要解决的问题。

sents.en: Depending on the minigame, these include the information available to the agent, visual ambiguity, the number of variables handled together, dependencies between decisions, planning depth, motion speed and timing windows, action precision, and recovery options.
sents.zh: 根据小游戏的不同，这些参数包括智能体可获得的信息、视觉模糊性、同时处理的变量数量、决策之间的依赖关系、规划深度、运动速度和时机窗口、操作精度以及恢复选项。

sents.zh: 更多的步骤、回合或等待本身并不会使配置变得更难。

sents.zh: 对于每一对相邻关卡，创建者必须说明智能体的决策或控制问题发生了什么变化。

sents.en: Table 5 shows the five levels of Rotating On-Screen Keyboard.
sents.zh: 表 5 展示了「旋转屏幕键盘」的五个关卡。

paragraphs.en: Section 2.4 defines the two interaction modes. For a fixed seed and difficulty, both modes generate the same world, information, goal, and action effects. The grader rejects actions submitted through the controls of the other mode. Table 6 shows examples.
paragraphs.zh: 第 2.4 节定义了两种交互模式。 对于固定的种子和难度，两种模式生成相同的世界、信息、目标和动作效果。 评分器会拒绝通过另一种模式的控件提交的动作。表 6 展示了示例。

sents.en: Section 2.4 defines the two interaction modes.
sents.zh: 第 2.4 节定义了两种交互模式。

sents.en: For a fixed seed and difficulty, both modes generate the same world, information, goal, and action effects.
sents.zh: 对于固定的种子和难度，两种模式生成相同的世界、信息、目标和动作效果。

sents.en: The grader rejects actions submitted through the controls of the other mode. Table 6 shows examples.
sents.zh: 评分器会拒绝通过另一种模式的控件提交的动作。表 6 展示了示例。

paragraphs.en: We revised minigames whose earlier versions did not require real-time interaction or allowed an agent to avoid it. For 64 minigames, a creator agent developed a new real-time minigame from the same source, as described in Section 2.2 . In 35 of these, the conversion removed the need for exploration, and a further revision restored it while keeping the goal, mechanic, and real-time execution. We also revised 23 minigames that already had real-time configurations, for instance to remove a brake that halts moving parts or to replace repeating motion that permits a precomputed solution. The remaining 13 minigames keep their original implementation, and Gym-Anything-RT uses the revised versions of all others.
paragraphs.zh: 我们修改了一些小游戏，其早期版本要么不需要实时交互，要么允许智能体规避实时交互。 对于其中64个小游戏，一个创建者智能体按照2.2节所述，从相同的源素材开发了一个新的实时小游戏。 在这些游戏中，有35个在转换后失去了探索需求，我们进行了进一步修订，在保留目标、机制和实时执行的前提下恢复了探索需求。 我们还修改了23个已有实时配置的小游戏，例如移除使运动部件停止的刹车，或替换允许预先计算解法的重复运动。 剩余的13个小游戏保留其原始实现，而 Gym-Anything-RT 对所有其他游戏使用修订后的版本。

sents.zh: 我们修改了一些小游戏，其早期版本要么不需要实时交互，要么允许智能体规避实时交互。

sents.zh: 在这些游戏中，有35个在转换后失去了探索需求，我们进行了进一步修订，在保留目标、机制和实时执行的前提下恢复了探索需求。

sents.zh: 我们还修改了23个已有实时配置的小游戏，例如移除使运动部件停止的刹车，或替换允许预先计算解法的重复运动。

paragraphs.en: Section 2.3 describes how we construct a non-real-time counterpart for each real-time minigame. The counterpart keeps the generator, goal, controls, difficulty parameters, available information, and grader of its real-time minigame, and changes only how the environment evolves over time. For example, in Rotating On-Screen Keyboard, the keyboard keeps its initial layout while the agent decides. In Clockwork Clutch Safe, each drive segment holds until the agent operates a clutch, and in Parallel Grillmaster, each food settles at its golden point once cooking starts. An independent audit agent compares the two versions across all ten configurations and returns any difference other than timing to the creator for repair. For the 35 minigames revised to restore exploration, we rebuilt the counterparts from the revised versions.
paragraphs.zh: 第2.3节描述了如何为每个实时小游戏构建一个非实时对应版本。 该对应版本保留其实时小游戏的生成器、目标、控制方式、难度参数、可用信息和评分器，仅改变环境随时间演化的方式。 例如，在旋转屏幕键盘（Rotating On-Screen Keyboard）中，智能体决策期间键盘保持其初始布局。 在发条保险箱离合器（Clockwork Clutch Safe）中，每段传动会一直保持直到智能体操作离合器；而在并行烧烤大师（Parallel Grillmaster）中，每种食物一旦开始烹饪就会定格在其最佳点上。 一个独立的审计智能体会对全部十个配置比较这两个版本，并将除时序之外的任何差异返回给创建者进行修复。 对于为恢复可探索性而修订的35个小游戏，我们基于修订后的版本重新构建了对应版本。

sents.zh: 第2.3节描述了如何为每个实时小游戏构建一个非实时对应版本。
